evidence.title: Governance of England
evidence.text: There has not been a government of England since 1707 when the Kingdom of England ceased to exist as a sovereign state, as it merged with the Kingdom of Scotland to form the Kingdom of Great Britain.

evidence.title: Governance of England
evidence.text: Kingdom of Great Britain continued from 1707 until 1801 when it merged with the Kingdom of Ireland to form the United Kingdom of Great Britain and Ireland, which itself became the United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland (UK) in 1922 (in reality; in name in 1927) upon independence for most of the island of Ireland.

evidence.title: Governance of England
evidence.text: The UK since then has gone through significant change to its system of government, with devolved parliaments, assemblies and governments in Scotland, Wales and Northern Ireland.

evidence.title: Governance of England
evidence.text: England, however, remains under the full jurisdiction, on all matters, of the Parliament of the United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland and the UK government as no devolved administration has been created for England within the new structure.

evidence.title: Governance of England
evidence.text: This situation has led to the anomaly, known as the West Lothian question, which is that Scottish Members of Parliament (MPs) are able to vote on legislation that affects only England whereas English MPs can not vote on certain Scottish matters due to devolution.

evidence.title: Governance of England
evidence.text: In some cases, such as top-up university tuition fees and foundation hospitals, the votes of Scottish MPs have been crucial in helping pass legislation for England that the majority of English MPs have opposed.

evidence.text: The United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland, commonly known as the United Kingdom (UK) and colloquially Great Britain (GB) or simply Britain, is a sovereign country in western Europe.

evidence.title: United Kingdom
evidence.text: Lying off the north-western coast of the European mainland, the United Kingdom includes the island of Great Britain, the north-eastern part of the island of Ireland and many smaller islands.

evidence.title: United Kingdom
evidence.text: Northern Ireland is the only part of the United Kingdom that shares a land border with another sovereign statethe Republic of Ireland.

evidence.title: United Kingdom
evidence.text: Apart from this land border, the United Kingdom is surrounded by the Atlantic Ocean, with the North Sea to its east, the English Channel to its south and the Celtic Sea to its south-south-west, giving it the 12th-longest coastline in the world.

evidence.title: United Kingdom
evidence.text: The Irish Sea lies between Great Britain and Ireland.

evidence.title: United Kingdom
evidence.text: With an area of 242500 km2 , the United Kingdom is the 78th-largest sovereign state in the world and the 11th-largest in Europe.

evidence.title: United Kingdom
evidence.text: It is also the 21st-most populous country, with an estimated 65.1 million inhabitants.

evidence.title: United Kingdom
evidence.text: Together, this makes it the fourth-most densely populated country in the European Union (EU).
